SMTO-PSM-0022 — A private saved parameter this task used has changed

GUID: a9a9cde0-39ed-424b-988c-ae23b1548b01
Slug: private-parameter-revision-missing
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • This task was set up with a private saved value, such as a password, that has since been edited or deleted. SMTO won't silently use the new version, so this task can't continue with it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check what the old task already did before it stopped, for example any change it made on a server. The old task may have finished some steps, and you don't want to repeat them in the new task.
  2. In Parameter Store, open the parameter the task used and make sure its current value is the one you want. The new task will use whatever is saved now, so it should be correct.
  3. Send your request again as a new message, typing @ and picking the parameter from the list. A new task saves the current version of the parameter, so it no longer depends on the old one.

What success looks like

  • The new task runs using the current parameter, and this error doesn't appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the parameter back to an old password just to make the old task continue.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A task's legacy private parameter binding could not be restored: the process-local copy is gone and the current Parameter Store record is missing or its updated_at differs from the accepted binding version.

What this means

  • Private binding resolution finds no exact record or its updated_at differs from the accepted binding version. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Private binding resolution finds no exact record or its updated_at differs from the accepted binding version.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare accepted key/version with the current stored record without substituting current credentials silently.

How to fix it

  • resolve() in src/agent_runtime/parameters/private_bindings.py only accepts the exact accepted revision. Restore that exact revision only if it is genuinely available; otherwise submit a new task that captures the current entry. Never swap a different secret into the accepted task.
  • Restore the exact accepted revision if available, or create a new task that explicitly captures the current parameter. Do not substitute a different secret into an accepted task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact accepted revision is restored, or new work explicitly accepts the intended current binding.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
